messages.author: 9cc042d8ce376c1f
messages.subject: support for sparse matrices?
parts: I don't see any mention of them in [the docs](https://r-nimble.org/html_manual/cha-RCfunctions.html).  Is there any support for sparse matrices?  If not, any advice on getting started making Nimble hooks for [existing sparse matrix C libraries](https://people.engr.tamu.edu/davis/suitesparse.html)?

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: support for sparse matrices?
parts:
Scott, briefly -- no, at present there is no native support for sparse matrix operations in nimble.  This is a goal of current development work, but be aware it's a long-term effort.

In order to interface with other existing sparse matrix C libraries, the nimbleExternalCall functionality might be what you're looking for.  This provides access to other (existing, compiled) C++ functions from inside nimbleFunctions.  See help(nimbleExternalCall) for more information and an example.  Fundamentally, you'll need the header (*.h) file and the compiled (*.o) object file.  With those in hand, you should be able to access the routines you're after from inside nimbleFunctions.

Let me know if this helps get you started in the right direction.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: 9cc042d8ce376c1f
messages.subject: Re: support for sparse matrices?
parts:
Daniel,

This is very helpful.  I noticed in the BayesNGP repository there are some functions exploiting sparse matrix logic.  Those functions seem to be relying on R's `sparseMatrix` support through `nimbleRcall` e.g. [here](https://github.com/danielturek/BayesNSGP/blob/master/BayesNSGP/R/SGV.R#L330).  

Do you have any insights into the performance tradeoff here vs trying to use an `nimbleExternalCall` to C++ level sparse libraries?  For example, were you able to avoid intermediate dense matrices?  When performing the MCMC, do the methods in BayesNSGP do an okay job of not creating too many copies of the original data and the covariance matrices?  Are there any other issues and gotchas that you might have run into by using `nimbleRcall` that you think might be avoidable by dropping down into a `nimbleExternalCall` instead?

I'm basically at the ground floor of my project, so I'm not entirely sure what the best path forward is, or what unknown unknowns to watch out for as I go.  Any advice is much appreciated.

Possibly @MarkDrisser has advice here as well?

Cheers,
-Scott

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: support for sparse matrices?
parts:
Scott, it's great that you're looking into this.  I have just a few comments to add.

There is some reasonable overhead for using nimbleRcall to access sparse matrix routines from R libraries, even when those routines simply call out to compiled code.  By my understanding, the overhead comes from the invocation of an R session, and everything that entails.  No, copies of the data are not made in this process, and things are never converted into a full dense matrix, so those are not issues, but there is overhead with invoking R.

If you have function prototypes and the compiled C++ object files for the sparse matrix routines that you wish to use from existing C++ libraries, then I believe nimbleExternalCall would perform significantly better.  It also does not involve making any copies or otherwise, but completely avoids calling out to an R session.  If you're just getting started and are truly looking for performance, then I would suggest you go this route.  Myself, or others on this list, should be able to help get this working if you run into problems.

Cheers,
Daniel
